To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
MSGCs are suitable for low-pressure operation in combination with 157 G d neutron convertors.

(a) the MSGCs are well suited to be operated in a two-stage amplification configuration with a 157 Gd neutron convertor, and that (b) the two-stage amplification scheme is superior to single stage operation with respect to gain and position resolution.
the MSGCs are optimized for low-pressure operation, using 157 Gd neutron convertors.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics: • Optimization of the detector gas mixtures with respect to the neutron convertor foams, • Development of a novel, robust, low-pressure detector technology with two closely spaced electrode layers, • Development of novel, high-resolution readout systems for the MSGCs and MDOT arrays, and • Development of a new detector concept for the imaging of the neutron flux distribution in the vicinity of a reactor core.
the development and construction of large-area, low-pressure MSGCs with 2D position readout for thermal neutron imaging using 157 Gd and 6 Li convertors.

the development of novel neutron imaging detectors with high spatial resolution, high detection efficiency and high counting rate capability, based on the use of large-area microstructure gas detectors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MSGCs and MDOT arrays, when operated in two-stage amplification, will be the ideal detector technology for the next generation of thermal neutron imaging detectors.

a large number of technical and technological problems have been solved, and that a novel generation of neutron imaging detectors with unsurpassed position resolution, high efficiency and low background has been developed.
a large-area neutron imager with a spatial resolution of ∼1 mm is within reach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the development and construction of a new detector generation for thermal neutron imaging has begun.
we have successfully developed a new type of neutron detector with unprecedented position and time-of-arrival resolutions, and with a high efficiency.

the development of large-area low-pressure microdot and microstrip gas chambers with two-stage amplification and composite neutron convertor foil for thermal neutron imaging is a challenging project, but it is also feasible.
The main takeaway from our work is that
large-area MSGCs can be produced at reasonable costs and with excellent spatial and temporal resolution.
the MSGC is an excellent detector for neutron imaging.
MSGCs can operate with gains >10 5 in 1 bar 157 Gd + 10 bar counting gas mixtures.
